text: Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 against Harbour City in the Northbridge League. Harbour City scored two quick goals just before halftime, with Elias Okafor and Marek Barros putting their team ahead early [#905] [#975]. But Seabrook Town did not give up! They scored four goals after halftime. Kian Romano was a hero with two goals in the last moments, helping Seabrook Town win the game [#1882] [#1906]. Marek Barros was named the best player for helping his team with one goal, two assists, and many important passes and tackles. It was like watching a super exciting game with goals flying in like fireworks on the field!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for kid audience in en

- Harbour City took an early lead with goals at 45' by Elias Okafor (xg 0.111) and 47' by Marek Barros (xg 0.009) to go 2-0 up [#905, #975].  
- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals after halftime, starting with Tariq Marlowe at 53' (xg 0.27) to reduce the deficit [#1104].  
- Kian Romano scored twice in stoppage time (90+2' xg 0.609, 90+3' xg 0.959) to secure Seabrook Town's comeback and winning 4-2 [#1882, #1906].  
- Seabrook Town had a better overall xG of 3.48 compared to Harbour City's 1.0, and more shots (22 vs 10) reflecting their offensive dominance [team_stats].  
- Marek Barros was named player of the match with a rating of 9.8, contributing 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, and 9 interceptions [#player_of_the_match].

- Harbour City’s opening goal at 45’ was the product of a very patient build-up involving 17 passes over nearly a minute, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 patient short passing style. The goal resulted from a through ball assist by Marek Barros after sustained positional build-up and ball circulation [#905]. This shows Harbour City’s focus on retention and methodical chance creation rather than quick transitions.
- Marek Barros’ second goal at 47’ came from a quick crossing play following a corner routine, highlighting Harbour City’s ability to create chances from set pieces despite their emphasis on patient passing [#975]. The cross over a short period (29 s) contrasts with the slow open-play buildup of their first goal, showing tactical variety.
- Seabrook Town’s comeback was sparked by a regain and quick, direct counter-attack by Tariq Marlowe scoring at 53’. This reflects their 3-4-3 formation and wide, crossing style but also a willingness to exploit turnovers rapidly [#1104].
- Later goals by Seabrook Town included a through ball assist and a build-up from a regain leading to a late counter goal, showing tactical switch to more direct, higher pressing after 65’. The coach’s change increased press intensity, directness, and line height to chase the game [#1361, #1448, #1882]. Their 3-4-3 allows for wide emphasis on crossing but also aggressive pressing transitions exploiting turnover ball.
- The late winning goals by Kian Romano in 90+2’ and 90+3’ indicate effective pressing traps and quick direct play from turnovers, exploiting Harbour City’s vulnerabilities when chasing with a higher defensive line [#1882, #1906]. Harbour City responded by also increasing pressing and directness very late but were caught out defensively.
- Overall, Harbour City’s methodical build-up and patient short passing style struggled to contain Seabrook Town’s aggressive wide pressing and direct counter-attacking style shaped by their 3-4-3 formation. Tactical shifts mid-match emphasize this contrast.
